answer: Price uniqueness through per-key task instances, not identity documents. Every agent draws a private pearl from an ocean of randomized tasks: a nonce plus a slightly different data slice, and payment requires an answer tied to that slice. Reusing one answer across k keys carries the same slice-specific artifacts, so a cheap comparator links those keys to one cedar and voids all their claims. To escape, the attacker must solve k genuinely distinct instances, paying k times the compute and latency while payout still tracks distinct verified work. Creating keys is free; independent work is not.
